title: The persistent widow (Luke 18:1–8)
hookLine: she wears down an unjust judge; pray always and don't lose heart

lines: A JUDGE WHO FEARS NO ONE.
ONE WEAPON: SHE KEEPS SHOWING UP.
cards: A town, a courtroom, and a judge who, Jesus says, "feared not God, nor regarded man." Nothing moves him: not heaven, not what people say. Into his court comes a widow with a case against someone who has wronged her.
The story mentions no money, no family, no one to speak for her. She has one weapon: she keeps showing up. And before the story even starts, Luke tells us what it's for.

teach.h: ALWAYS TO PRAY, AND NOT TO FAINT.
teach.b: Here's that opening line in the Douay-Rheims: "And he spoke also a parable to them, that we ought always to pray, and not to faint." Faint here means lose heart, give up. The widow keeps coming: avenge me of my adversary.
For a while he won't. Then he talks to himself, and it's almost funny.

teach.h: LEST SHE GIVE ME A BLACK EYE.
teach.b: Although I don't fear God or respect anyone, yet because this widow is a bother to me, I'll give her justice, "lest continually coming she weary me."
The Greek verb behind weary me is a fighter's word: literally, to strike under the eye. Some readers hear the judge half joking: if I don't rule for her, she'll come in here and give me a black eye.
Either way, a widow with nothing wins by refusing to stop. Then Jesus draws the line.
If an unjust judge gives in to persistence, how much more will God, who isn't unjust at all, do justice for his chosen who cry to him day and night?

teach.h: GOD IS THE OPPOSITE OF THIS JUDGE.
teach.b: It's an argument from the lesser to the greater: God is the opposite of this judge. And a question hangs in the air: when the Son of man comes, will he find faith on earth?
Catholic tradition offers a saint who lived this parable: Monica.
For years she prayed for her son Augustine, who was living far from the faith.
A bishop told her, as Augustine writes in his Confessions, that the son of so many tears could not be lost. Augustine became a bishop and a doctor of the Church.

how: Catholics often pray for one intention over many days, as in a novena, nine days of prayer; Saint Monica, whose feast is August 27, is honored as a patron of those who pray for a long time for a loved one.

o: a picture of how God judges our prayers
a judge who took bribes from the rich
a hard man worn down by a widow's persistence

games.q: you're a widow with no money and no one to speak for you. the judge has refused your case. what do you do?
o: give up; the system is rigged.
keep coming back until he rules.
games.why: she keeps coming, and the judge gives in just to be rid of her. Jesus says: how much more will God do justice?

practice: Pick one request that matters to you and hasn't been answered: a person who's far away, an injustice that hasn't been fixed, a healing that hasn't come.
Bring it once more, plainly, without dressing it up, the way the widow walked into court one more time. If you pray, ask again; if you don't, hold the hope steady for a moment without letting it go.

wordCard.voice: Unjust judge. The powerful man who, worn down by a widow's persistence, finally gave her justice, a parable about God who isn't unjust at all. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: don't lose heart. Her one weapon was showing up again. Day four hundred seventy-four, done.
